source.text: לִשְׁלֹמֹ֨ה׀אֱֽלֹהִ֗ים מִ֭שְׁפָּטֶיךָ לְמֶ֣לֶךְ תֵּ֑ן וְצִדְקָתְךָ֥ לְבֶן־מֶֽלֶךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Of Solomon. God, your judgments to the king give, and your righteousness to [the] son of [the] king.

en.L: Of Solomon. \q God, give {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} judgments to the king, \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness to the king's son.
en.B: Of Solomon. \q God, grant the king {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} justice, \q and the king's son {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} righteousness.
en.R: By Solomon. \q God, help the king to judge fairly, as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do. \q Help the king's son to do what is right, as {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} do.

decisions.choice: The title shares verse 1
decisions.reason: This psalm's title is short and the Hebrew counts it together with the first line as verse 1, so here the verse numbers are the same as in Bibles that print the title without a number.

decisions.choice: of Solomon: for or by Solomon
decisions.reason: Only this psalm and Psalm 127 bear Solomon's name. "Of" may mean he wrote it or that it is about or for him; verse 20 closes "the prayers of David", and the ancient Greek translation reads "for Solomon", as a prayer for the new king.

decisions.choice: the king, the king's son: the same person
decisions.reason: The two lines name one king twice: he is king, and he is the rightful heir of a king, of David's line.

decisions.choice: your judgments: your just decisions
decisions.reason: The word (mishpatim) is the decisions of a judge. The king rules well only if God gives him God's own justice (1 Kings 3:9-12).

decisions.choice: the king: a human king of David's line, read later of the Messiah
decisions.reason: The psalm prays for the king in Jerusalem, a son of David (verses 1, 20). His reign of justice, peace and worldwide rule goes beyond any king Israel had, and later Jewish and Christian readers took it as a picture of the Messiah. The New Testament does not quote it, but the gifts of the wise men in Matthew 2:11 echo verses 10-11 and 15 (with Isaiah 60:6). Pronouns for the king here are not marked as pronouns for God.

decisions.choice: By Solomon
decisions.reason: As with "By David" in other titles, Readable uses plain words; the sense of "of" is uncertain (m2).

source.text: יָדִ֣ין עַמְּךָ֣ בְצֶ֑דֶק וַעֲנִיֶּ֥יךָ בְמִשְׁפָּֽט׃

records.literal_gloss: May he judge your people with righteousness, and your afflicted with justice.

en.L: May he judge {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people with righteousness, \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} afflicted with justice.
en.B: May he govern {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people rightly, \q and {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} poor with fairness.
en.R: May he rule {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} people fairly. \q May he do what is right for {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} poor people.

decisions.choice: may he judge: a prayer for the king
decisions.reason: The verbs in verses 2-17 can be read as wishes or as statements about the future. Several are clearly wishes (verses 8, 15-17), so the psalm is read as a prayer throughout; verses 12-14 give its reasons.

decisions.choice: your afflicted: God's poor and oppressed people
decisions.reason: The poor belong to God, and the king's first duty is to do right by them (verses 4, 12-14).

source.text: יִשְׂא֤וּ הָרִ֓ים שָׁ֘ל֥וֹם לָעָ֑ם וּ֝גְבָע֗וֹת בִּצְדָקָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: May [the] mountains bear peace to the people, and [the] hills, in righteousness.

en.L: May [the] mountains bear peace for the people, \q and [the] hills, in righteousness.
en.B: May the mountains yield well-being for the people, \q and the hills bring it through righteousness.
en.R: May the land, from the mountains to the hills, give the people a good life, \q because the king does what is right.

decisions.choice: peace: well-being, plenty
decisions.reason: The word (shalom) is peace in the full sense: safety, health and good harvests. The hill country of Israel bears this when the king rules justly (verse 16).

decisions.choice: in righteousness: through the king's just rule
decisions.reason: The land's plenty comes by way of righteousness, the right order the king keeps.

decisions.choice: because the king does what is right
decisions.reason: Readable names the righteousness as the king's (m2).

source.text: יִשְׁפֹּ֤ט׀עֲֽנִיֵּי־עָ֗ם י֭וֹשִׁיעַ לִבְנֵ֣י אֶבְי֑וֹן וִֽידַכֵּ֣א עוֹשֵֽׁק׃

records.literal_gloss: May he judge [the] afflicted of [the] people; may he save [the] children of [the] needy and crush [the] oppressor.

en.L: May he judge the afflicted of the people; \q may he save the children of the needy \q and crush [the] oppressor.
en.B: May he defend the poor among the people \q and bring rescue to needy families; \q may he break the oppressor in pieces.
en.R: May he stand up for poor people. \q May he save the children of those in need. \q May he crush anyone who mistreats them.

decisions.choice: judge: give justice to, defend
decisions.reason: To judge the afflicted is to take up their case and see them treated rightly (10:18; 82:3).

decisions.choice: the children of the needy: needy people
decisions.reason: "Children of" can mean the members of a group; here the needy and their families.

source.text: יִֽירָא֥וּךָ עִם־שָׁ֑מֶשׁ וְלִפְנֵ֥י יָ֝רֵ֗חַ דּ֣וֹר דּוֹרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: May they fear you with [the] sun, and before [the] moon, generation of generations.

en.L: May they fear {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} as long as [the] sun [endures], \q and before the moon, generation [after] generations.
en.B: May people stand in awe of {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} as long as there is a sun and a moon, \q from one generation to the next.
en.R: May people honor {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} for as long as the sun and moon are in the sky, \q for all time.

decisions.choice: may they fear you
alternatives: may he live long (the ancient Greek translation)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew reads "may they fear you", that is, God, whose justice the king carries out. The ancient Greek translation read a word with almost the same letters, "may he continue", which keeps the king as the subject.

decisions.choice: with the sun and before the moon: as long as they last
decisions.reason: The sun and the moon stand for what lasts (89:37-38).

source.text: יֵ֭רֵד כְּמָטָ֣ר עַל־גֵּ֑ז כִּ֝רְבִיבִ֗ים זַרְזִ֥יף אָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: May he come down like rain on mown grass, like showers, drops of [the] earth.

en.L: May he come down like rain on mown grass, \q like showers [that] water [the] earth.
en.B: May he be like rain falling on a cut field, \q like showers soaking the land.
en.R: May the king be good for his people, like rain that falls on a field after the hay is cut, \q like showers that water the ground.

decisions.choice: mown grass: a field after cutting
decisions.reason: The word (gez) is a mowing or a shearing (Judges 6:37). Rain on a field just mown brings new growth.

decisions.choice: drops: a soaking
decisions.reason: The word (zarzif) is found only here and seems to mean a downpour.

decisions.choice: May the king be good for his people
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means: a good king refreshes his people as rain does a field (2 Samuel 23:3-4).

source.text: יִֽפְרַח־בְּיָמָ֥יו צַדִּ֑יק וְרֹ֥ב שָׁ֝ל֗וֹם עַד־בְּלִ֥י יָרֵֽחַ׃

records.literal_gloss: May [the] righteous flourish in his days, and abundance of peace until [the] moon is no more.

en.L: May [the] righteous flourish in his days, \q and abundance of peace until the moon is no more.
en.B: In his days may the righteous thrive, \q and peace overflow until the moon is gone.
en.R: While he is king, may people who do what is right do well. \q May there be peace everywhere for as long as the moon shines.

decisions.choice: the righteous
alternatives: righteousness (some Hebrew manuscripts and ancient translations)
decisions.reason: Some manuscripts and ancient translations read "righteousness", which pairs with "peace" as in verse 3. The text here has "the righteous".

decisions.choice: until the moon is no more: for ever
decisions.reason: As in verse 5, the moon stands for what lasts.

source.text: וְ֭יֵרְדְּ מִיָּ֣ם עַד־יָ֑ם וּ֝מִנָּהָ֗ר עַד־אַפְסֵי־אָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: And may he rule from sea to sea, and from [the] River to [the] ends of [the] earth.

en.L: And may he rule from sea to sea, \q and from the River to [the] ends of [the] earth.
en.B: May his rule stretch from sea to sea, \q from the River to the far ends of the earth.
en.R: May he rule over all the land between the seas, \q from the Euphrates River to the farthest places on earth.

decisions.choice: the River: the Euphrates
decisions.reason: "The River" is the Euphrates, the far edge of the land promised to Abraham (Genesis 15:18; Exodus 23:31).

decisions.choice: Zechariah 9:10
decisions.reason: Zechariah 9:10 repeats this line of the king who brings peace, "his rule from sea to sea, and from the River to the ends of the earth".

decisions.choice: the Euphrates River
decisions.reason: Readable names the river (m1).

source.text: לְ֭פָנָיו יִכְרְע֣וּ צִיִּ֑ים וְ֝אֹיְבָ֗יו עָפָ֥ר יְלַחֵֽכוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: Before him may desert-dwellers bow, and his enemies lick dust.

en.L: Before him may [the] desert-dwellers bow down, \q and his enemies lick [the] dust.
en.B: Let the nomads of the desert kneel before him, \q and let his foes lick the dust.
en.R: May the people who live in the desert bow down to him. \q May his enemies fall on their faces in the dirt.

decisions.choice: desert-dwellers: the peoples of the wilderness
alternatives: his foes (a change of one letter)
decisions.reason: The word (tsiyyim) means those who live in dry places, people or animals (74:14). Some read "foes", which pairs with "enemies".

decisions.choice: lick the dust: bow to the ground in defeat
decisions.reason: Defeated enemies lay face down before the victor (Isaiah 49:23; Micah 7:17).

decisions.choice: fall on their faces in the dirt
decisions.reason: Readable says what the picture means (m2).

source.text: מַלְכֵ֬י תַרְשִׁ֣ישׁ וְ֭אִיִּים מִנְחָ֣ה יָשִׁ֑יבוּ מַלְכֵ֥י שְׁבָ֥א וּ֝סְבָ֗א אֶשְׁכָּ֥ר יַקְרִֽיבוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] kings of Tarshish and [the] coastlands tribute may they bring back; [the] kings of Sheba and Seba a gift may they bring near.

en.L: May [the] kings of Tarshish and [the] coastlands pay tribute; \q may [the] kings of Sheba and Seba bring gifts.
en.B: Let Tarshish and the coastlands send their kings with tribute; \q let the kings of Sheba and Seba bring him presents.
en.R: May kings from faraway lands across the sea pay him taxes. \q May kings from Sheba and Seba in the south bring him gifts.

decisions.choice: Tarshish, the coastlands, Sheba, Seba: the far ends of the known world
decisions.reason: Tarshish lay far to the west across the sea (Jonah 1:3), the coastlands are the islands and shores of the Mediterranean, Sheba was in southern Arabia, and Seba probably in Africa (Isaiah 43:3). Kings from west and south bring gifts.

decisions.choice: the queen of Sheba; Matthew 2:11
decisions.reason: Solomon received gifts from the queen of Sheba (1 Kings 10:1-10). Christian readers have seen these verses fulfilled in the wise men who brought gifts to the child Jesus (Matthew 2:11).

decisions.choice: faraway lands across the sea
decisions.reason: Readable says where the places are (m1) rather than naming them all.

source.text: וְיִשְׁתַּחֲווּ־ל֥וֹ כָל־מְלָכִ֑ים כָּל־גּוֹיִ֥ם יַֽעַבְדֽוּהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And may all kings bow down to him, all nations serve him.

en.L: And may all kings bow down to him; \q may all nations serve him.
en.B: Let every king bow low before him \q and every nation be his servant.
en.R: May all the kings of the world bow down to him. \q May every nation serve him.

decisions.choice: bow down: lie face down in homage
decisions.reason: The verb (hishtachavah) is the bow of a subject before a king, or of a worshiper before God.

decisions.choice: all kings, all nations: a rule over the whole world
decisions.reason: The prayer asks for more than any king of Israel had; it reaches toward the reign promised to David's son (2:8; 89:28).

source.text: כִּֽי־יַ֭צִּיל אֶבְי֣וֹן מְשַׁוֵּ֑עַ וְ֝עָנִ֗י וְֽאֵין־עֹזֵ֥ר לֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: For he will deliver [the] needy [one who] cries for help, and [the] afflicted, and [one who] has no helper.

en.L: For he will rescue [the] needy [one who] cries for help, \q and the afflicted, and [the one who] has no helper.
en.B: For he rescues the needy when they cry out, \q and the poor who have no one else to stand by them.
en.R: He will rescue poor people when they call to him for help. \q He will save those who have no one else to help them.

decisions.choice: for: the reason for the nations' homage
decisions.reason: Verses 12-14 give the reason kings will honor him (verses 8-11): he cares for the helpless. Here the verbs read best as statements.

decisions.choice: the needy, the poor (plural)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has one needy person, drawn as a type. Balanced and Readable say "the needy ... they", so the line is plainly about anyone in need; Literal keeps the singular.

source.text: יָ֭חֹס עַל־דַּ֣ל וְאֶבְי֑וֹן וְנַפְשׁ֖וֹת אֶבְיוֹנִ֣ים יוֹשִֽׁיעַ׃

records.literal_gloss: He will have pity on [the] weak and needy, and [the] lives of [the] needy he will save.

en.L: He will have pity on [the] weak and [the] needy, \q and he will save the lives of the needy.
en.B: He feels for the weak and the needy, \q and he saves the lives of those in need.
en.R: He cares about people who are weak and poor. \q He saves their lives.

decisions.choice: have pity: be moved to spare
decisions.reason: The verb (chus) is to look on with pity and spare someone from harm.

source.text: מִתּ֣וֹךְ וּ֭מֵחָמָס יִגְאַ֣ל נַפְשָׁ֑ם וְיֵיקַ֖ר דָּמָ֣ם בְּעֵינָֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: From oppression and from violence he will redeem their life, and precious [is] their blood in his eyes.

en.L: From oppression and from violence he will redeem their life, \q and their blood will be precious in his eyes.
en.B: He sets them free from cruelty and violence; \q their lives are of great worth in his sight.
en.R: He saves them from people who mistreat them and hurt them. \q To him their lives are very valuable.

decisions.choice: redeem: act as their protector and rescue them
decisions.reason: The verb (ga'al) is used of a near relative who buys back a family member or avenges his blood (Leviticus 25:25). The king acts as next of kin to the poor.

decisions.choice: their blood is precious: their lives are of great worth
decisions.reason: He will not let their blood be shed as if it cost nothing (116:15).

source.text: וִיחִ֗י וְיִתֶּן־לוֹ֮ מִזְּהַ֪ב שְׁ֫בָ֥א וְיִתְפַּלֵּ֣ל בַּעֲד֣וֹ תָמִ֑יד כָּל־הַ֝יּ֗וֹם יְבָרֲכֶֽנְהֽוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: And may he live, and may [one] give to him from [the] gold of Sheba, and may [one] pray for him continually; all the day may [one] bless him.

en.L: And may he live, and may [one] give him from the gold of Sheba; \q and may [one] pray for him continually; \q all the day may [one] bless him.
en.B: May the king live! Let him receive Sheba's gold; \q let prayer be made for him always, \q and blessing asked for him all day.
en.R: May the king live a long life! May people give him gold from Sheba. \q May they always pray for him. \q May they ask God to bless him every day.

decisions.choice: he, one: the king lives; others give, pray and bless
alternatives: the poor man lives, and the king gives him gold
decisions.reason: "May he live" is the cry for a king (1 Samuel 10:24). The other verbs have no named subject and are read as "people". Some take verse 15 as going on from verse 14, the rescued poor man living and the king giving to him.

decisions.choice: the king
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable name the king, so the line is clear after verse 14.

decisions.choice: ask God to
decisions.reason: To bless the king here is to ask God's blessing on him.

source.text: יְהִ֤י פִסַּת־בַּ֨ר׀בָּאָרֶץ֮ בְּרֹ֪אשׁ הָ֫רִ֥ים יִרְעַ֣שׁ כַּלְּבָנ֣וֹן פִּרְי֑וֹ וְיָצִ֥יצוּ מֵ֝עִ֗יר כְּעֵ֣שֶׂב הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: May there be abundance of grain in the land, on [the] top of [the] mountains; may its fruit wave like Lebanon, and may they flourish from [the] city like [the] grass of the earth.

en.L: May there be abundance of grain in the land, on [the] top of [the] mountains; \q may its fruit wave like Lebanon, \q and may [people] flourish from [the] city like the grass of the earth.
en.B: Let grain grow thick across the land, right up to the hilltops; \q let its harvest rustle like the trees of Lebanon, \q and let city people spring up like grass in the fields.
en.R: May the land grow plenty of grain, even on the tops of the hills. \q May the crops sway in the wind like the great forests of Lebanon. \q May the towns be full of people, like fields full of grass.

decisions.choice: abundance: plenty
decisions.reason: The word (pissah) is found only here; it is usually taken as "abundance".

decisions.choice: like Lebanon: like its great forests
decisions.reason: Lebanon was famous for its tall cedar forests (104:16). The grain is to stand as thick and tall, waving in the wind.

decisions.choice: may they flourish from the city: may the people of the cities thrive
decisions.reason: The subject is not named; it is taken as the people, growing in number like grass (Job 5:25).

source.text: יְהִ֤י שְׁמ֨וֹ לְֽעוֹלָ֗ם לִפְנֵי־שֶׁמֶשׁ֮ יִנּ֪וֹן שְׁ֫מ֥וֹ וְיִתְבָּ֥רְכוּ ב֑וֹ כָּל־גּוֹיִ֥ם יְאַשְּׁרֽוּהוּ׃

records.literal_gloss: May his name be forever; before [the] sun may his name increase; and may they bless themselves by him, all nations; may they call him blessed.

en.L: May his name be forever; \q as long as [the] sun [endures] may his name increase; \q and may [people] bless themselves by him; \q may all nations call him blessed.
en.B: May his name live on forever, \q his fame spread as long as the sun shines. \q May all nations ask to be blessed as he is blessed, and call him happy.
en.R: May people always remember the king's name, for as long as the sun shines. \q May all nations be blessed because of him. \q May they all say how blessed he is.

decisions.choice: may it increase: the word as read, not as written
decisions.reason: The written and read forms are two spellings of a rare verb meaning to sprout or grow; the sense is the same.

decisions.choice: Genesis 12:3; 22:18
decisions.reason: The nations blessing themselves by the king echoes God's promise that all nations would be blessed through Abraham and his offspring (Genesis 12:3; 22:18). To bless oneself by someone is to pray, "May I be blessed like him".

decisions.choice: call him blessed: call him happy, fortunate
decisions.reason: The verb ('ashar) is from the same root as "How blessed" (1:1).

decisions.choice: be blessed because of him
decisions.reason: Readable gives the plain outcome of the wish (m2).

source.text: בָּר֤וּךְ׀יְהוָ֣ה אֱ֭לֹהִים אֱלֹהֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֑ל עֹשֵׂ֖ה נִפְלָא֣וֹת לְבַדּֽוֹ׃

records.literal_gloss: Blessed [be] YHWH God, [the] God of Israel, who does wonders by himself.

en.L: Blessed [be] {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God, the God of Israel, \q who alone does wonders.
en.B: Blessed be {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God, Israel's God; \q only {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} works wonders.
en.R: Give thanks to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} God, Israel's God! \q He alone does amazing things.

decisions.choice: the praise that closes Book Two
decisions.reason: Verses 18-20 are not part of the psalm itself. They close the second of the five books of the Psalms (Psalms 42-72), as 41:14 closes the first, 89:53 the third and 106:48 the fourth.

decisions.choice: blessed: praised
decisions.reason: To bless God (barukh) is to speak well of him, to give him thanks and praise, as in 41:14.

decisions.choice: wonders: God's amazing acts
decisions.reason: As in 71:17.

source.text: וּבָר֤וּךְ׀שֵׁ֥ם כְּבוֹד֗וֹ לְע֫וֹלָ֥ם וְיִמָּלֵ֣א כְ֭בוֹדוֹ אֶת־כֹּ֥ל הָאָ֗רֶץ אָ֘מֵ֥ן׀וְאָמֵֽן׃

records.literal_gloss: And blessed [be] [the] name of his glory forever, and may the whole earth be filled [with] his glory. Amen and amen.

en.L: And blessed [be] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glorious name forever, \q and may the whole earth be filled [with] {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory. \q Amen and amen.
en.B: Blessed be {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glorious name for all time; \q may {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory fill all the earth. \q Amen and Amen.
en.R: Praise {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} wonderful name forever! \q May {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} glory fill the whole world. \q Amen! Amen!

decisions.choice: Numbers 14:21; Isaiah 6:3
decisions.reason: The hope that God's glory will fill the earth is in Numbers 14:21 and Isaiah 6:3 (also Habakkuk 2:14).

decisions.choice: Amen: so be it
decisions.reason: Amen means "it is true, let it be so"; the double Amen ends Books One to Three (41:14; 89:53).

source.text: כָּלּ֥וּ תְפִלּ֑וֹת דָּ֝וִ֗ד בֶּן־יִשָֽׁי׃

records.literal_gloss: Ended are [the] prayers of David, son of Jesse.

en.L: Ended are the prayers of David son of Jesse.
en.B: Here end the prayers of David son of Jesse.
en.R: This is the end of the prayers of David, Jesse's son.

decisions.choice: the end of a collection of David's prayers
decisions.reason: This note closed an earlier collection of David's psalms. More psalms of David come later in the book (86; 101; 103; 108-110; 138-145), so it marks the end of a collection, not of all his psalms.

decisions.choice: prayers: psalms
decisions.reason: The word (tefillot) is prayers; here it names the psalms as a whole, which are prayers and praise to God.
